The search for life in the Universe has a signiﬁcant focus on M dwarf stars, as they are the 52 most common stellar type,1 and their small sizes and low masses make it easier to detect 53 and characterize small, temperate planets. However, M dwarfs, especially those with the 54

lowest masses, emit frequent ﬂares for long portions of their lifetimes that may erode plan- 55 etary atmospheres.2,3 Demographic studies have shown that planets the size of Earth in the 56 Habitable Zone — the region where liquid water could likely exist on planetary surfaces — 57 are common.4,5 But only a handful of such worlds have been measured to be rocky, and all 58 of them orbit active, lower-mass M-dwarfs, so the survival of their atmospheres is question- 59 able. Here, we report new exoplanet mass measurements from radial velocity observations 60 with the VLT/ESPRESSO spectrograph of TOI-700, a relatively quiet, early M dwarf star 61 that hosts 4 small planets, including 2 in the star’s Habitable Zone.6–9 We ﬁnd that TOI-700 62 c (2.65 R⊕) is a low-mass (2.5 M⊕) planet, which must have a hydrogen/helium dominated 63 atmosphere given its low bulk density (0.73 g cm−3). Furthermore, the small (1.16 R⊕), Hab- 64 itable Zone planet, TOI-700 d, has a mass of 2.4 M⊕, implying a rocky composition. Given 65 that TOI-700 c and d have similar masses, the presence of TOI-700 c, a puffy sub-Neptune, 66 orbiting interior to the Habitable Zone planets, implies that d might be able to maintain a 67 heavier, secondary atmosphere as these planets were subjected to the same stellar history. 68

M dwarf stars are valuable targets for exoplanet detection and subsequent characterization; 69 as a result of these stars’ low masses and radii, planets of a given size and irradiance produce com- 70 parably larger signals in transit photometry, radial velocity (RV), and transmission spectroscopy as 71 compared to planets orbiting higher mass stars. Furthermore, M dwarf stars make up the majority 72 of stars in the Milky Way, comprising 70% of stellar content.1 With their long lifetimes, M dwarf 73 stars have a broad range of ages we can study, and even the oldest M dwarf systems are still on the 74 Main Sequence today. Literature has shown that planets are common around M dwarf stars,4 so M 75 dwarf planets are abundant targets. An open question in the ﬁeld is whether small, temperate plan- 76 ets orbiting low-mass M dwarfs in particular are able to retain their atmospheres over time,10–15 as 77 M dwarfs are known to be highly magnetically active for signiﬁcant portions of their lifetimes.2,3 78

TOI-700 (TIC 150428135) hosts 4, small transiting planets (from interior and moving out- 79 ward - b, c, e, d with radii of 0.94, 2.65, 0.93, and 1.16 R⊕, and orbital periods of 9.98, 16.05, 80 27.81, and 37.42 days, respectively) discovered using data from NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Sur- 81 vey Satellite (TESS) mission.6,8,16 TOI-700 is an M2.5 dwarf star (Vmag = 13, M = 0.415M⊙, R = 82 0.421R⊙) located 31.1 pc away from the Sun that resides in TESS’s Southern Continuous Viewing 83 Zone. We obtained 183 high-resolution spectra of TOI-700 using the ESPRESSO spectrograph17,18 84 on ESO’s 8.2-meter Very Large Telescope (VLT). 85

We constructed a 4-planet model to jointly ﬁt the transit photometry as well as the radial 86 velocities and the FWHM of the RV cross correlation functions using pyaneti.19 We used a 87 multi-dimensional Gaussian Process to model the stellar activity simultaneously with the Keplerian 88 signals from the planets. The TOI-700 system contains planets on either side of the exoplanet Radius Valley that sepa- 99 rates rocky, Super Earth planets from gaseous sub-Neptune worlds, making it an advantageous test 100 bed for theories on how the Radius Valley formed.23 One of the leading theories is photoevapora- 101 tion of planetary atmospheres. In this theory, planets form with hydrogen/helium envelopes, which 102 are then eroded by high energy radiation from the host star. New research has shown that the 103 Radius Valley may become shallower and less distinct with decreasing stellar mass and increasing 104

4


<!-- Page 8 -->


planet orbital period as a result of more varied planetary compositions, resulting in a wider range of 105 resulting radii after undergoing photoevaporation.24–26 Further observations (mass measurements 106 in particular) are required in order to better understand this effect. 107

We investigated whether the TOI-700 system architecture is consistent with having been 108 shaped by photo-evaporative mass loss using the escape model, EvapMass.27 EvapMass is 109 designed to analyze multi-planet systems, thereby alleviating the need to know the full stellar 110 EUV/x-ray history as it is shared between the planets, and assumes that all planets form with a 111 hydrogen/helium dominated envelope. Then, it compares planet sizes, assumes that a planet in 112 or below the Radius Valley has lost its envelope, and estimates the minimum mass necessary for 113 a planet to maintain its atmosphere, thus ending up on the larger side of the Radius Valley. We 114 found that at 2.50 ± 0.34 M⊕, TOI-700 c’s mass is too low for the system have been shaped by 115 photoevaporation alone. Rather the combination of planet c’s volatile-rich composition and planet 116 d’s rocky composition require different, or additional, mass loss mechanisms to explain TOI-700’s 117 system architecture. Possible explanations include that TOI-700 d ﬁnished forming later than TOI- 118 700 c, after the hydrogen in the disk dissipated, or that TOI-700 d experienced giant impacts late 119 in planet formation.28–32 120

The presence of a low-density, sub-Neptune interior to planets e and d in the TOI-700 system 121 indicates that the high energy emission of TOI-700 was insufﬁcient to completely strip the atmo- 122 sphere from planet c, and ergo, also suggests that planets e and d may have maintained higher mean 123 molecular weight secondary atmospheres that would be even less susceptible to photoevaporation- 124 driven mass loss. If true, this would stand in stark contrast to early results from JWST observations 125 of TRAPPIST-1 b and c, small, rocky planets orbiting an M dwarf that are consistent with the plan- 126 ets being bare rocks with no secondary atmospheres.14,33 127

We currently have a limited population of well-characterized, small, temperate planets upon 128 which to test theories of atmosphere evolution; these planets’ longer orbital periods make them 129 both less likely to transit and result in smaller RV signals, making these worlds challenging to 130 detect. Currently, with measured radii via photometry34 and masses via transit timing variations35 131 showing rocky planet compositions, the temperate worlds of the TRAPPIST-1 system are among 132 the most promising targets for searching for atmospheres on small, temperate planets. The TOI- 133 700 system now provides a second M dwarf system where at least one of the temperate, Earth-sized 134 planets in the system has a rocky composition. 135

Unlike TRAPPIST-1, an old (7.6 ± 2.2 Gyr),36 very low-mass M dwarf star (0.08 M⊙)34 136 that still ﬂares regularly, TOI-700 is a younger (3.86 ± 0.72 Gyr37), early M dwarf star (0.415 137 M⊙) that shows no evidence of ﬂares over several years of optical photometry and spectroscopic 138 observations. Earlier-type M dwarfs spin down faster, and their activity decreases much earlier in 139 their lifetimes than lower mass M dwarfs.2,38 It is possible that the more rapid decrease in activity 140 for more massive, partially-convective M dwarfs allows planets to maintain their atmospheres. Methods 163

System History: TOI-700 b, c, and d were originally discovered using time series photometry 164 from NASA’s TESS mission16 in 2020.6,7 Later, an additional planet, TOI-700 e, was found to 165 orbit in between TOI-700 c and d (thus the out-of-order planet names), and the planet properties 166 were revised with an additional year of TESS data in 2023.8 Since this publication in 2023, TESS 167 has re-observed TOI-700, yielding an additional 9 sectors of photometry covering 27 days each. 168

Stellar Characterization: The star was initially characterized photometrically.6 In particular, the 169 metallicity was estimated using metal-sensitive photometric color combinations that were cali- 170 brated using stars with accurate metallicities from near-IR spectra.6 Spectroscopic characterization 171 was carried out on the newly obtained ESPRESSO spectra using ODUSSEAS, 41 which is designed 172 speciﬁcally to determine [Fe/H] and Teff of M dwarfs by measuring pseudo equivalent widths for 173 more than 4000 stellar absorption lines in optical spectra. The photometrically and spectroscopi- 174 cally derived Teff and log g agreed, well within 1-σ. [Fe/H] varies slightly from the photometrically 175 derived values, and we report both values for [Fe/H] in Table 1. For all other stellar parameters, 176 we adopt the parameters outlined in previous literature.8 177

UV Characterization of TOI-700 with Hubble Space Telescope: The Hubble Space Telescope 178 (HST) observed TOI-700 in January 2021 (Program ID: 16207; PI: Arney) with the COS and STIS 179 instruments, covering 1300-5600 ˚A. Spectra were obtained with the low-resolution COS/G140L, 180 STIS/G230L, and STIS/G430L gratings with total effective exposure times of 27,178 seconds, 181 10,261 seconds, and 300 seconds, respectively. The UV spectra were obtained in time-tag mode. 182 We reduced the spectra using standard tools and procedures provided by STScI. We detected emis- 183 sion from common chromospheric and transition region ions and continuum emission from the 184 stellar photosphere at wavelengths longer than ∼2600 ˚A. We measured the following emission 185 line ﬂuxes for C II (1334.5, 1335.7 ˚A), Si IV (1393.8, 1402.8 ˚A), C IV (1548.2, 1550.8 ˚A), He II 186 (1640.5 ˚A), and Mg II (2796.4, 2803.5 ˚A): 3.0, 1.7, 5.1, 2.5, and 56.1 (units of 10−16 erg cm−2 s−1 187 and integrated over all multiplet transitions). No corrections were made to the C II or Mg II ﬂuxes 188 to account for attenuation from the interstellar medium, an effect that could mean those ﬂuxes are 189 underestimated by up to about 30% depending on the line of sight through the local interstellar 190 medium.42–44 The fractional line luminosities (i.e., log L(line)/Lbol) corresponding to the above 191 listed ions) are -6.40, -6.65, -6.17, -6.48, and -5.13. These values are in family with other ﬁeld-age 192 M2.5V stars.45 No ﬂares or other stellar variability were detected in the UV spectral time-series, 193 which is unusual for an M dwarf.46 However, the count rate for this star was very low, so the data 194 cannot rule out weaker ﬂares that are more readily detected from brighter M dwarfs. 195

Stellar Age and Activity: TOI-700 was detected by the eROSITA X-ray observatory as source 196 1eRASS J062822.4-653442 47 with an X-ray ﬂux of fX = 1.337×10−17 W m−2 (0.2-2.3 keV energy 197 range) at separation 6′′.08 from TOI-700’s optical position with 1-σ X-ray positional error 2′′.98 198 (2.04σ away). The density of eROSITA X-ray sources in the vicinity of TOI-700 (at separations 199 < 1◦) is 1.9 × 10−5 arcsec−2, so the probability of an unrelated interloper X-ray source appearing 200 within 6′′.08 is approximately 0.0022 (1 in 458). Predicted Stellar Evolution for TOI-700: We inferred the past evolutionary history of the star 206 based on a MIST V1.2 theoretical stellar evolutionary track49 for protosolar composition (an ap- 207 proximation given the estimated metallicity and age), and measured empirical high energy (X-ray, 208 UV →”XUV”) activity-age trends for age-dated M dwarfs.48,50 As a 0.415 M⊙pre-main sequence 209 star, TOI-700 would have gravitationally contracted from a 1 Myr-old ∼0.5L⊙T Tauri star along 210 a convective Hayashi track to the Main Sequence, and its fusion reactions would have halted its 211 dimming in bolometric luminosity by age 290 Myr,49 with this time of minimum luminosity prac- 212 tically deﬁning the star’s pre-Main Sequence contraction timescale.51 Since arriving on the Main 213 Sequence, TOI-700 is only predicted to have increased its bolometric luminosity by 7% by age 4 214 Gyr. 215

TESS Time Series Photometry: TESS16 is an all-sky survey that launched in 2018 that is designed 216 to detect exoplanets via the transit method. TESS has (4) 24x24 degree wide-ﬁeld cameras stacked 217 vertically to create a combined 24x90 degree ﬁeld-of-view with a pixel scale of 21′′/pixel. TESS 218 tiles the sky in 27-day sectors, with overlapping regions at the ecliptic poles, creating 2 Continuous 219 Viewing Zones (CVZs). TOI-700 lies within TESS’s Southern CVZ and has been observed for 220 extended periods of time over the course of the TESS mission. TOI-700 was observed for 11 221 sectors in Cycle 1 (Aug. 2018 - July 2019), 10 in Cycle 3 (July 2020 - May 2021), and 9 sectors 222 in Cycle 5 (Feb. 2023 - Sept. 2023).
